page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-64 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 256 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1 instruction/data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core and cryptographic capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier performance in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and Passmark CPU scores, alongside strong results in database operations and Redis SET operations, which reach 63.14 million operations per second. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth is highly efficient at 4074.06 GB/sec, uncached large-block read and write speeds fall into the average tier. Cryptographic execution is supported by hardware-accelerated AES and VAES instruction sets, yielding strong Passmark encryption test results.

The lack of local storage and GPU acceleration introduces specific architectural tradeoffs. While the instance performs well in text generation for small language models, it exhibits poor performance for large-scale LLM text generation, dropping to 2.41 tokens per second on a 70B model. This profile makes the n2d-standard-64 highly suitable for general-purpose enterprise workloads, multi-threaded software compilation, database operations, and web serving, whereas deep learning training and large-scale model inference are better suited for GPU-accelerated alternatives.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-64 is a general-purpose server configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256 GB of RAM, running on an AMD EPYC 7B13 x86_64 processor. It features 32 physical cores with multithreading, 32 MB of L3 cache, and lacks local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks show strong multi-core processing, database operations, and Redis throughput, alongside high cached memory bandwidth. However, uncached memory operations and large-scale LLM text generation perform average to poor. This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for balanced, compute-heavy enterprise workloads, multi-threaded compilation, and database hosting, but is not designed for GPU-dependent tasks or massive local storage requirements.
